## Site Response { #sec-MPAF}

The estimation of dynamic site response can be achieved by utilizing a scalar amplification factor that is dependent on the average shear-wave velocity $\bar{v}_S$, as outlined in ASCE/SEI 7-22. For a target service level, defined by the Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP), and a given structural period $T_n$, the median spectral ordinates $S_a(T_n,\bar{v}_S)$ expected at sites characterized by an average shear-wave velocity $\bar{v}_S$, can be derived from the spectral ordinates on rock, denoted as $ S_a(T_n)^o$. This approach facilitates a tailored response analysis based on arbitrary geotechnical site conditions.


$$S_a(T_n,\bar v_S) \approx F(T_n,\bar v_S) \ S_a(T_n,v_{ref})$${#eq-SAS}

where $F(T_n,\bar v_S)$ is the multi-period site factor and $S_a(T_n,v_{ref})$ is the spectral ordinate for the structural period $T_n$ in rocks (A) or firm soils (BC). The model proposed by @Stewart2017 is a three-component model dependent on shear-wave velocities $\bar v_S$ and can be used for both hard rock with $v_{ref}$ of 3000 m/s or soft rock with $v_{ref}$ of 760 m/s reference values.

$$\mathrm{ln}\ F \approx \beta_{BC} +\beta_{A} +\beta_{NL}+\varepsilon$${#eq-AF}

where $\beta_{BC}$ is a scaling term relative to $\bar v_S$ = 760 m/s, $\beta_{A}$ is amplification at $\bar v_S$ = 760 m/s relative to $v_{ref}$ = 3000 m/s and $\beta_{NL}$ is a factor that considers non-linear effects, which has strong influence in soft-soil conditions. 

The error term $\varepsilon$ from [@Stewart2017] is a log-normal random variable, with mean $E[\varepsilon]\approx 0$ and variance $\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon]\approx \sigma_F^2$. Because the spectral ordinates in rock are actually random variables, with conditional expectation $s_a(T_n)$ and variance $\sigma_A^2$, the error term from this model has been adapted to incorporate the seismic hazard's uncertainty:

$$\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon]\approx \sigma_F^2+\sigma_{A}^2$$
